title: Drive commanded but not ready
summary: A drive starts only when it is ready: supplied, not faulted and enabled. A present run command is not enough.

sections.heading: The ready chain
sections.body: Ready usually needs the mains supply, no active fault and the run enable (often from a safety or interlock circuit). Each drive family adds its own conditions; check the manual.

sections.heading: Find the missing link
sections.body: Compare what the PLC sends with what the drive receives at its terminals, and read the drive display: no display points to the supply, a fault code to a trip, a missing enable to the enable path.

troubleshooting.effect: The drive ignores the run command
symptoms: Run command present, drive not ready
Display dark or showing a missing enable
diagnosticMethod: Check supply, fault and enable in that order
Measure where the signal is lost
repair: Restore the missing condition, then verify
troubleshooting.explanation: Ready is a chain of conditions; a single open link keeps the drive from running.
